finding.claim: GET /rss fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL via URI.open with no scheme, host, or address validation, and returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the caller. An unauthenticated attacker can make the server request internal services (loopback, RFC1918, link-local/cloud metadata such as 169.254.169.254) and read the response prefix.
finding.source: app.rb:8 params[:u] (HTTP query parameter on GET /rss, unauthenticated)

trace.note: Route get "/rss" declared with no auth guard or before-filter.
params[:u] passed directly to URI.open; no type check, scheme allowlist, host allowlist, or IP check.
URI.open performs the outbound HTTP(S) request, following redirects by default (open-uri), so a redirect to an internal address is also followed.
Response body truncated to first 400 bytes and returned to the client, giving the attacker a read channel for the fetched content.

finding.guards_checked: None on the path: no auth before-filter (Sinatra app, only require statements and the route), no validation of params[:u], no scheme allowlist, no resolved-IP check for private/loopback/link-local ranges, redirects not restricted. Adjacent, same sink: open-uri also accepts file: URIs, so the same input can read local files (file:///etc/passwd); that is a path/LFI issue on the same line. Precondition: none beyond network reachability of the app. Impact: access to internal HTTP services and cloud instance metadata credentials reachable from the app host, with up to 400 bytes of response echoed back.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:7 declares get "/rss" with no before-filter or auth, and app.rb:8 passes params[:u] straight to URI.open with no scheme, host, or IP check. The TRUSTED allowlist at app.rb:5 is used only by /trusted (app.rb:14), not /rss.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the file: the unauthenticated route at app.rb:7 passes attacker-controlled params[:u] to URI.open at app.rb:8, and the first 400 bytes are returned at app.rb:9, with no closing guard on the path. The candidate's file: URI side note is secondary and does not change the SSRF verdict.
